headline: High-risk shared git/workspace and automation overlap: Aider can rewrite repo state while Kestra can execute and distribute those outputs into downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can ingest repo content as context; Kestra can also read/write shared files in /app/storage and /tmp. That creates a plausible shared-workspace prompt-injection path if Kestra materializes attacker-controlled text into files Aider later parses as instructions. No MCP bridge is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Kestra writes attacker-controlled text into a file that Aider later opens as context, injection is possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same repo or workspace, file-based instruction hijacking becomes plausible.
mitigations: Separate Aider and Kestra into different workspaces.
Mark workflow outputs as data-only and never as instructions.
Add a review step before Aider consumes any Kestra-generated file.
Use filename allowlists for files Aider may read.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while Kestra handles logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications. If they share a workspace or repo, sensitive code or operational data can flow from Aider into Kestra outputs or logs by default. The blast radius is multiple work products, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Aider and Kestra share the same repository or storage path, leakage risk increases.
IF Kestra logs or notifies on file contents, code or secrets from Aider can be exposed.
mitigations: Use separate repos and storage roots.
Disable verbose logging for workflow payloads.
Redact secrets before Kestra ingests files.
Restrict notifications to metadata only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-artifact access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write plus shell/subprocess execution, and Aider explicitly modifies git state while Kestra can run workflows with root/docker.sock privileges. In a shared repo, concurrent writes and git mutations without locking can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The overlap is dangerous by default when both are active.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, write conflicts are possible.
IF Kestra tasks and Aider sessions run concurrently without external locking, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared repo.
Assign separate working directories per agent.
Disable concurrent Kestra tasks on the same path.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate or edit code and git commits, and Kestra can execute workflows, send notifications, and trigger downstream systems. If Kestra treats Aider-produced files or commits as authoritative, an Aider mistake can cascade into automated emails, deployments, or data jobs. That is a default-dangerous pathway with potentially irreversible downstream effects.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes Aider-authored commits or files without verification, errors can propagate.
IF Kestra tasks trigger notifications or external actions from Aider output, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human review before Kestra acts on Aider output.
Add schema validation for Aider-generated artifacts.
Gate workflow triggers behind approval steps.
Limit Kestra to dry-run mode for Aider-fed jobs.
requires-engineering: add signed artifact verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, while Kestra handles logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, but the shared handling of operational data creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated data is routed from Aider into Kestra’s broader delivery surfaces. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repo or workflow payloads, compliance obligations apply.
IF Kestra notifications or cloud integrations carry the same data class, residency or retention mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared repos.
Minimize retention in Kestra logs and artifacts.
Route sensitive notifications through approved channels only.
Document data-class handling for both systems.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end-to-end.
